Subject: SIG/CAIQ + DPIA scope for proposed integration

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. MediPartner's procurement and compliance teams need to run Redwood through an information security review (SIG / CAIQ) and a scoped DPIA before we can sign. The specific asks in our RFP are:

- Completed SIG/CAIQ questionnaire (or evidence equivalent)
- DPIA scoped to LLM usage for PHI-like data in the EU (high level flow + risk mitigations)
- Confirmation on whether customer-provided prompts/responses are used to train models, and an opt-out proof workflow
- Sample retention mapping including prompt/response TTL and how redaction/ephemeral storage is enforced
- KMS and key custody description and where keys reside for EU tenants

Can you share an initial evidence bundle and let us know timeframe? We need the materials for our legal/compliance review by Sep 16.

Regards,
Clara Nguyen

compliance@medipartner.com

Hi Clara —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: we do not use customer prompts or responses from your tenant to train models by default; we provide an explicit opt-in for training and a documented opt-out workflow. For an EU healthcare deployment we recommend Private (VPC) or Dedicated with EU-only routing + customer-managed KMS.

I've looped in Neha (Privacy/Legal) and Marissa (Solutions) to scope the DPIA and gather the SIG/CAIQ evidence. Initial plan:
- I'll attach a scoped DPIA flowchart and a redaction/retention summary (PDF/CSV) for your team to review.
- Neha will provide the formal statement on 'no-train' and sample log extracts showing opt-out enforcement.
- Marissa will prepare SCC clause mapping and details on hosted vs. private key custody.

Estimated delivery: first-pass bundle by Sep 9, finalized by Sep 14. If you need anything earlier, let us know which items are highest priority.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ + DPIA scope for proposed integration

Hi Clara and team —

Following Ben's note, here are focused responses to the DPIA / privacy items you listed. I've attached redwood-dpia-scoped-flowchart.pdf and a CSV sample of access logs with sensitive columns redacted.

1) Training on customer data
- Default behavior: No customer data (prompts, completions, attachments) from tenant-managed workloads is used to update or fine-tune any models.
- Opt-in: Customers may explicitly opt in to allow anonymized contribution to a training pool; this is a contract-level setting and requires affirmative action via Console + signed amendment.
- Evidence: We can provide config snapshots showing tenant training flag = false, and redacted audit records demonstrating enforcement.

2) Opt-out workflow proof
- Workflow: Tenant sets 'no_train=true' at the project level (UI/API). Requests with that flag are tagged and routed to inference instances with training-disabled enforcement.
- Enforcement evidence: sample audit logs (attachment) showing request IDs, project IDs, and the enforcement tag. We can additionally provide HMAC-signed attestations for one-day windows.

3) Retention & ephemeral handling
- Prompts: default TTL 30 days for hosted, configurable to 0 (ephemeral) for Dedicated/Private.
- Responses: stored for 7 days by default for debugging; can be disabled.
- Redaction: PII/PHI filtering can be applied at ingest via built-in redaction rules or customer-managed middleware. Ephemeral mode stores only hashed metadata and a minimal stub for troubleshooting.

4) KMS & key custody
- EU Private: customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) via supported KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) and optional HSM integration. Keys never leave the customer-managed KMS in Private deployments. Hosted customers may use Redwood-managed keys or BYOK depending on contract.

5) SCC / contractual mapping
- Marissa will attach a mapping spreadsheet with relevant SCC clauses and how Redwood's controls map to them. For EU healthcare we recommend Dedicated or Private to simplify SCC attestation scopes.

Next steps: Ben/Marissa will share the SCC mapping and a DocuSign amendment template for opt-in/opt-out training choices. Clara — once you confirm which items you want in the immediate bundle (SIG vs full CAIQ vs only DPIA + logs), we'll prioritize.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

(Attachments: access-logs-sample-202708.csv stub — columns redacted; redwood-dpia-scoped-flowchart.pdf stub)
